optimizedCv.targetRoleTitle: Digital Product Manager, Developer Tools Platform

professionalSummary.text: Digital Product Manager with experience owning the roadmap for deployment services on an internal developer tools platform, driving a 22% increase in automated deployments from 62% to 84% within three months.
professionalSummary.witness: The share of deployments completed without manual intervention rose from 62 percent to 84 percent in the three months after the automated rollback release, per the platform's monthly deployment report against its documented baseline of 62 percent.

professionalSummary.text: Led eight deployment-service release reviews, maintaining decision logs that documented deferred items and rationale, with platform engineering and consuming teams.
professionalSummary.witness: Chaired the review for all eight deployment-service releases that year and kept the decision log, including what was deferred and why.

professionalSummary.text: Collaborated with platform engineering and engineering teams to set backlog priorities, with decisions documented in release planning sessions.
professionalSummary.witness: Set the direction for the deployment service on the internal developer tools platform; every sprint I settled the backlog order with platform engineering and a rotating group of the engineering teams that depend on the service.

professionalSummary.text: Maintained up-to-date release notes documenting limitations (e.g., automated rollback coverage gaps) and on-call hand-over information for platform operations.
professionalSummary.witness: Kept the release notes current; they record, for instance, that automated rollback does not yet cover database migrations, and carry the hand-over notes the platform on-call rota relies on.

experienceHighlights.text: Automated rollback release drove 22% increase in automated deployments (62% to 84%) within three months, meeting documented baseline targets.
experienceHighlights.witness: The share of deployments completed without manual intervention rose from 62 percent to 84 percent in the three months after the automated rollback release, per the platform's monthly deployment report against its documented baseline of 62 percent.

experienceHighlights.text: Chaired eight deployment-service release reviews, maintaining decision logs with deferred item rationale.
experienceHighlights.witness: Chaired the review for all eight deployment-service releases that year and kept the decision log, including what was deferred and why.

experienceHighlights.text: Set backlog priorities with platform engineering and consuming teams through sprint planning sessions.
experienceHighlights.witness: Set the direction for the deployment service on the internal developer tools platform; every sprint I settled the backlog order with platform engineering and a rotating group of the engineering teams that depend on the service.

experienceHighlights.text: Documented release limitations (e.g., database migration coverage gaps) and maintained on-call hand-over notes in release documentation.
experienceHighlights.witness: Kept the release notes current; they record, for instance, that automated rollback does not yet cover database migrations, and carry the hand-over notes the platform on-call rota relies on.

projectsAndWorkSamples.text: Monthly deployment report showing 62% to 84% automated deployment increase, with baseline and rollback release marked; decision log for rollback release included.
projectsAndWorkSamples.witness: Work sample: a year of the monthly deployment report (share of deployments without manual intervention, the baseline and the rollback release marked) together with the decision log for the rollback release; report identifiers are included for tracing.

skills.text: Roadmap ownership for deployment services, backlog prioritization with platform engineering and consuming teams, release review leadership, and metrics-driven improvement of deployment automation.
skills.witness: Set the direction for the deployment service on the internal developer tools platform; every sprint I settled the backlog order with platform engineering and a rotating group of the engineering teams that depend on the service. Chaired the review for all eight deployment-service releases that year and kept the decision log, including what was deferred and why. The share of deployments completed without manual intervention rose from 62 percent to 84 percent in the three months after the automated rollback release, per the platform's monthly deployment report against its documented baseline of 62 percent. Kept the release notes current; they record, for instance, that automated rollback does not yet cover database migrations, and carry the hand-over notes the platform on-call rota relies on.

optimizedCv.evidenceBoundary: The materials establish the candidate's direct involvement in setting direction, backlog prioritization, release reviews, metrics improvement, and release documentation as described in the job requirements. The materials do not establish the candidate's role in 'lining up each release with platform engineering and the consuming teams' beyond the decision-making process, as the candidate states that dates and rollout order were platform engineering manager's decisions.

decisionBoundary.statement: All requirements are supported by evidence, but the candidate's role in 'lining up releases' requires clarification on whether they initiated or merely documented the process.
